details: For every binary concept class, $\mathrm L(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{RL}(\mathcal H).
proof: Induct on the finite Littlestone dimension d. At the root of any shattered tree, the two restrictions have dimensions a,b at most d, and they cannot both equal d (otherwise their complete trees join to give dimension d+1). Thus $a\leq d$ and $b\leq d-1$ after ordering. Induction bounds each subtree's randomized value by its Littlestone dimension, so the root tree has half its expected branch length at most $1/2+(a+b)/2\leq d$. Taking suprema proves the claim; the infinite case follows by truncation.
proof_source: The randomized-tree definition is Definition 1 of \cite{filmus2023randomized}; the comparison is a direct induction.
witness_verification: On the singleton-plus-empty class, Littlestone dimension is 1 whereas randomized Littlestone dimension is 1-2^{-n}, which is strictly smaller for every n>=1.
name: Littlestone Dimension / Randomized Littlestone Dimension
